cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Truth or Loyalty
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between protecting the relationship and answering a dangerous question honestly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. The client asked who wrote our pitch. Will you tell her I copied it, or protect our partnership? Please.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I'll withdraw it. Will you keep my name out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked whether you copied it. Withdrawing doesn't answer her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then before you say yes, decide whether we're still partners when she puts down the phone.

mechanism: A leads client damage control and offers to withdraw the pitch while forcing B to choose honest disclosure or preserving their partnership.
confusable: Unlike merely asking for a cover story, A makes the relationship itself the cost of truth; borrowed authority absorbs a practical burden to keep B on side.
comparison: A professional copying accusation differs from family loyalty over a broken vase.
seedUse: D130-b copied pitch, joint withdrawal and direct client question; S02-b adjusts who handles withdrawal to retain B cooperation.
